_comment: What Home Assistant's USB lists do not say and the kit needs: which serial protocol a stick speaks (family), its serial settings, and on a two-port adapter which port is the radio. Keyed by 'VID:PID description-glob' exactly as the list has it. 'proven' = served, synced and failed over on real hardware by this project; everything else is taken from public documentation and NOT yet verified on a stick ('served only' until someone proves it). guest/lib/zradio-usb-ids.py merges this with Home Assistant's lists into usb-ids.json, at install time. In 'add': confirm=true = a generic bridge chip, a radio only if it answers the probe; beside=<kind> = counts only when the same device's other port answered as that kind.
_commit_comment: The Home Assistant core commit whose USB lists the install reads (its zha, zwave_js, homeassistant_sky_connect and homeassistant_connect_zbt2 manifests). Moving it is a reviewed change: the tests' copies of those files (tests/fixtures/ha-core) move with it, and CI checks the two agree.

10C4:8A2A *z-wave*.note: Nortek HUSBZB-1: port 0 is the Z-Wave radio.

add.note: A CP2105 two-port bridge with a generic product string: port 1 is the Z-Wave controller. Any other CP2105 device matches too — the probe decides.
Port 0 of the same bridge: the stick's Zigbee radio. Not probed (no EZSP probe yet): a Zigbee stick that answers a probe is preferred over it.
